title: The anchoring gate: the reference walks, and the filter inversion
question: Model the hub's two known sensor behaviors (bias walk, rate filter) — does the sim then explain run 27's transfer failure?
headline: The bias walk is modeled and REFUTES run 27's prime suspect (the drift punishes the old policy, not the candidate). Modeling the 30 ms rate filter uncovered a stark inversion: the real robot NEEDS the filter, the sim robot cannot TOLERATE it (classical falls 6/6 at zero delay) — the sim is structurally too lag-fragile, and that is now the top sysID target.
hub_output: -- sim experiment; drift eval = 8 eps/condition, filter probe = 6 eps --
drift 0.2-0.4 dps: old policy terminates 6-8/8 (walks out); 8M candidate 0 falls, unchanged
filter 30ms: classical falls 6/6 at delay 20ms, 10ms, and 0ms; old policy falls 6/6
filter 15ms: classical 0/6 falls -- the sim cliff sits between 15 and 30 ms of rate lag
hardware: the same 30ms filter is load-bearing for every controller (runs 16, 22, 26)
